name: Local Deep Research
tagline: A self-hosted deep-research assistant that searches the web, academic databases, and your own documents, then writes a cited report
seoTitle: Local Deep Research - Private Self-Hosted Research Assistant
metaDescription: Local Deep Research (LDR) is an open-source AI research assistant that runs on your own machine: any local or cloud LLM, 10+ search engines, and an encrypted personal library.
overview: Local Deep Research (LDR) is an open-source research assistant you run yourself. You give it a complex question; it plans the searches, runs them across the web, academic databases and your own documents, and synthesises what it finds into a report with citations back to the sources it used.

The project's emphasis is control and privacy. It works with any local or cloud LLM — llama.cpp, Ollama, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint — and pairs with search back-ends you choose, so a fully local setup (Ollama plus a self-hosted SearXNG) never sends a query off your machine. The README states the project contains no telemetry, analytics or tracking, and each user's data lives in an isolated SQLCipher database encrypted with AES-256 whose key is derived from their password; the password itself is never stored, so login works by attempting to decrypt the database.

Beyond one-off questions, LDR builds a knowledge base that compounds. Sources it turns up — arXiv preprints, PubMed articles, web pages — can be downloaded into an encrypted library, where the text is extracted, indexed and embedded, so later research runs can query your own accumulated documents alongside the live web.
features: Multiple research strategies, from quick pipeline modes for fast facts to a fully agentic `langgraph-agent` mode in which the LLM decides what to search, which specialised engine to use, and when to synthesise
10+ search back-ends including SearXNG, arXiv, PubMed and Semantic Scholar, plus your own private documents
Model-agnostic: llama.cpp, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible cloud endpoint
A personal library that downloads, extracts, indexes and embeds sources so past research is searchable in future runs
Per-user SQLCipher AES-256 encrypted databases, with per-user LLM API keys stored encrypted inside them rather than in a shared server-level store
Ships as a Docker image, a Docker Compose stack, or a pip package with a web UI on port 5000

gettingStarted.intro: LDR needs three pieces: an LLM endpoint, a search engine, and LDR itself. The Docker Compose route brings up a CPU-only stack on any platform; the pip route is the lightest if you already run Ollama and SearXNG.

steps.heading: Run the Docker Compose stack
steps.body: Fetch the project's compose file and start it. This is the recommended path on macOS and Windows, where the `--network host` flag used by the plain `docker run` recipe does not work.

steps.heading: Or install from PyPI
steps.body: Install the package and start the web UI. You will still need Ollama (or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and SearXNG running — the project's pip install guide has the full recipe.
steps.code:
pip install local-deep-research
python -m local_deep_research.web.app   # starts the web UI on http://localhost:5000

steps.heading: Bring your own LLM and search engine
steps.body: For a fully local setup, run Ollama for inference and SearXNG for search, then point LDR at the SearXNG instance.
steps.code:
docker run -d -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama
docker exec ollama ollama pull gpt-oss:20b
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 --name searxng searxng/searxng

steps.heading: Open the UI and pick a strategy
steps.body: Browse to http://localhost:5000 after about 30 seconds. In Settings, select `langgraph-agent` for the autonomous agentic mode, which adaptively switches between search engines and collects more sources than the pipeline strategies.

useCases: Running deep research on sensitive questions without sending queries or documents to a hosted provider
Literature review across arXiv, PubMed and Semantic Scholar with citations back to each source
Building a private, searchable library of papers and web pages that later research runs can draw on
Getting cited research reports out of a local model on consumer hardware instead of a frontier API
